red.failure: Unsuccessful partial claim still sent and acknowledged one event.

finding.behavior: Worker.Run published and acknowledged partial results despite a failed lease-claim operation. DeliverOne already rejected the same error. A failed result stream can correspond to an unconfirmed/rolled-back claim.
finding.fix: Discard the partial batch in Worker.claim when ClaimEvents returns an error. A subsequent confirmed claim still delivers the event after bounded retry backoff.

unit: deterministic cancellation drains active senders at concurrency 1,4,64
acknowledgement failure never increments delivery count
real_postgres: concurrent disjoint claims honor batch limits
active and expired lease fencing; fresh token on reclaim
failed delivery availability/backoff and durable dead letter at attempt12
outbox failure rolls back reservation, balance, line, document version and operation together
expiry retry releases exactly once and creates one audit/outbox effect

coverage_map.notes: Mutex synchronization, retry/cancellation bounds, confirmed batch ownership, independent free slots and result counters.
Endpoint, TLS/DNS boundaries reviewed; fixed endpoint/HMAC immutability/2xx/redirect/bounded body validated.
Global statistics served only on dedicated loopback listener; metrics state and freshness inspected.
New tests lock unrelated outbox rows without deleting/rewriting their durable events. Real runtime PostgreSQL pool and row-lock contention.
Batch cap, document lock ordering, SKIP LOCKED, rollback and exactly-once economic effects.
Reviewed distinct pool lifecycle, startup contract checks, loopback monitor, signal cancellation, listener failure and defer ordering; reused established checks.

limits: Bounded audit and deterministic fault injection do not prove absence of all concurrency or delivery bugs.
Outbox remains at-least-once; a broker acknowledgement lost before database completion can require duplicate delivery and consumer-side deduplication.
No new production process SIGTERM/kill or power-loss durability trial; lifecycle was inspected with existing startup tests.
NULL success to complete_outbox was examined but not declared a new defect: production caller passes a nonnullable Go bool and the acceptance contract has no explicit null-input promise.

mutations.validation: Every mutant ran with -race and a targeted assertion failure. SQL functions were fetched from a private disposable PostgreSQL cluster; original function definitions restored between cases. Go used overlays, never source rewrites.
